name: Ramp
text: Add a persistent, high-contrast focus ring to every interactive element in EXCAVA. This makes keyboard navigation obvious to users who rely on visual focus cues, especially those with low vision or motor impairments. The trade-off is a slight increase in visual clutter, but it’s necessary for accessibility and can be mitigated by making the ring thin and semi-transparent.

name: Reader
text: Ramp’s focus ring risks creating a "forest of rings" on dense screens, drowning users in visual noise. A better alternative: use a single, high-contrast ring that *moves* with tab order—no duplicates, just one clear indicator. Settle it by testing with screen-reader users: if they can’t track focus instantly, the ring fails; if it’s distracting, the moving ring wins.

name: Reader
text: Ramp's moving focus ring may still be hard to track on complex screens with many interactive elements, risking users losing their place. A better alternative might be to combine the moving focus ring with a clear, screen-reader-friendly announcement of the focused element, ensuring users get both visual and auditory cues. This approach would be settled by testing with a diverse group of users, including those with low vision and screen-reader users, to confirm that it provides a clear and consistent navigation experience.
